country.name: France
country.kicker: A national idea with an international life.

overview.summary: A European republic whose influence reaches through institutions, language, design, and culture. France is both deeply embedded in Europe and geographically present far beyond it through overseas territories.
overview.geography: Metropolitan France meets the Atlantic, the English Channel, and the Mediterranean. The Alps and Pyrenees help frame its borders. Overseas France also reaches the Americas, Indian Ocean, and Pacific.

whyItMatters.title: A shaper of European cooperation
whyItMatters.text: A founding participant in European integration, France helps shape decisions that extend across the European Union.

whyItMatters.title: Culture as lasting influence
whyItMatters.text: French language, art, food, and ideas about public life travel through education, institutions, and communities worldwide.

stories.question: Why does Paris loom so large?
stories.summary: Centuries of political power and cultural investment accumulated in one place.

sections.title: A center built over time
sections.text: Royal courts, national institutions, universities, and cultural collections helped concentrate influence in Paris. The city’s landmarks contain successive layers of French history.

sections.title: A city that became a model
sections.text: Nineteenth-century rebuilding created boulevards, parks, and urban forms that influenced cities elsewhere. France’s regional identities nevertheless extend far beyond the capital.

stories.takeaway: Paris is a powerful lens on France, but never the entire picture.

scene.mapNote: A capital near northern European connections, within a much larger country.

stories.question: How did France help build a shared Europe?
stories.summary: After devastating wars, cooperation became a practical political project.

sections.title: Make conflict less likely
sections.text: Early European integration linked strategically important industries. France was among the founding countries of the communities that preceded today’s European Union.

sections.title: Shared decisions, national debates
sections.text: A single market and the euro tie France to neighboring economies. What should be decided nationally or collectively remains an active political question.

stories.takeaway: Europe is not just somewhere France is located. It is an institutional project France helped create.

scene.mapNote: Close neighbors became partners in a shared European system.

stories.question: Why is France on more than one continent?
stories.summary: The familiar European outline is only part of the state.

sections.title: The legacy of an empire
sections.text: French colonial expansion left territories and communities around the world. Decolonization changed those relationships, but did not produce one uniform outcome.

sections.title: Different constitutional arrangements
sections.text: French Guiana, Réunion, and other overseas places have differing legal statuses. Their people, environments, and local histories complicate any simple definition of “mainland France.”

stories.takeaway: A country’s territory, culture, and history can stretch beyond the outline most maps teach us.

scene.mapNote: French Guiana lies on the Atlantic coast of South America.
